deviations_from_the_spec: Fixture folders are named after the script without extension (fixtures/snap/, fixtures/witness/) following CONTRACT 5 (tcb/fixtures/<name>/); the brief's <script-name> could also mean snap.mjs/. Witness fixtures are data files (fixtures/witness/<group>/cases.json) that one corpus run turns into cards and snapshots; test names carry the behaviour id (T4 for normalization, T2/T3/T5/T7/T21 for basic, T6 for number-variants).

The tests do not use helpers.mjs (not yet written and not mine): each test file carries its own small makeRoot, thresholds writer, canonical-JSON/sha256 and ledger-chain verifier (hash = sha256(prev + canonical(line without hash)), per CONTRACT 3.7). If the library's canonical form differs for some value, the ledger check in T1/T9/T10/T11/T15/T16/T18 will show it.

The pure-function tests the witness spec mentions (normalize, numberTokens, witnessCard) are not written as direct calls: their signatures are in neither spec nor contract. T4, T5 and T6 go through the command line with data cases instead. T-import only checks that importing witness.mjs does nothing and that the three names are functions.

T14 case 2 (redirect to http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/ with loopback disallowed for that hop) is ambiguous: with allow_loopback true the spec makes mapped loopback allowed. I test the redirect to http://10.0.0.1/ with loopback allowed, and a direct http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:PORT/ with allow_loopback false (server must get no request).

T14 address table runs through `--new` with one invented card per address (one process, one row per address in result.urls) and adds more members of the listed ranges (169.254.169.254, 192.168.x, 172.16/12, 192.0.2.x, 203.0.113.x, 224/4, ::, ff02::1, 2001:db8::1 and mapped, 6to4 and NAT64 forms of 192.168.0.1).

Extra behaviours taken from the spec's steps and tested under extra ids: T2b (gzip, deflate, br decoding), T3b (header charset, meta charset, UTF-8 default), T10 exact-cap body stored, T11b (deadline covers the body), T12 five redirects still followed, T5 before-the-quote window (near and far), T8b (blocked-only retrievals, missing meta, missing text file, later failed retrieval does not hide earlier text), T10b (by-url source_changed), T11 ids sorted, T12b (other usage errors), T-missing (exit 2 missing), T-param-missing (exit 2 param-missing).

Assertions that go beyond the exact spec wording and may need the builder's confirmation: stdout `ok` is true only for exit 0; exit 2 outcomes of snap carry reason `unverifiable`; the witness `pass` check line has exactly one reason (range); witness T15 expects the rejected record to be written before the exit 3 (as the spec says) and exactly one incident line; `retrieved_at` in meta and by-url equals the --now value; an empty root (no coord, no thresholds) is enough for the exit 66 tests, and the script must create nothing in it.
not_testable_without_the_app: snap: real web pages (extraction quality, paywalls, 200-answering challenge pages, real PDFs): skipped test 'needs the app'.
snap: that a real run has allow_loopback false (selftest's threshold check): skipped test 'needs the app'.
witness: the G7 share of honest cards whose reader saw only a fetch summary and whose quote is a paraphrase (pilot measure): skipped test 'needs the app'.
witness: witnessing quotes from real pages: skipped test 'needs the app'.
open_points: snap T14 'allowed' half (93.184.216.34 and [2606:2800:220:1::] pass the filter) is a skipped test: a run against a public address would use the network, and the spec exports no filter function to call without it. Reason in the skip text.

witness pure-function behaviours cannot be called directly (see deviations): normalize, numberTokens, witnessCard signatures are unspecified, so their semantics are covered only through the command line.

I could not run the tests against the scripts: tcb/scripts/ does not exist yet. I ran `node --check` on both test files and ran both files once; they load, build fixtures and servers, and fail only with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the missing scripts. I also checked that every quote_at and number_at in the three cases.json files occurs in its text. No leftover temp roots remained.

Ambiguities flagged for the builder: (1) whether a witness record for a rejected card carries quote_offset (I assert offsets only for witnessed cards); (2) the exact bound distance for a number before the quote (I test 55 and 407 characters, not the edge); (3) whether a CRLF after a hyphen counts as a line break (case n-hyphen-line-break-crlf assumes yes); (4) whether guillemets map to the double quote (case n-angle-quotes assumes yes); (5) whether the sign character is part of number_offset (not asserted for sign cases).

The tests assume a Windows PowerShell at the contract's proc_exe path to get the start time of the sleeper process for T20 (snap) and T17 (witness); if it cannot be read, those two tests skip themselves with a reason rather than fail.

T14b relies on a preload (fixtures/snap/spy-net.mjs, node --import, env SNAP_SPY_OUT set only for the child) that wraps http(s).request/get, dns.lookup and fetch and probes the lookup of each request's agent. It sees an agent only if the script passes it via the request options (agent.options.lookup or a lookup option); a script that builds connections some other way would fail T14b and need the test adjusted.

Concurrency: each file runs its tests 3 at a time (describe concurrency 3); every script run starts PowerShell once for its lock identity, so a slow machine may need a longer per-run timeout than the 120 s the helpers use.
